note: Values copied from the sources named here; make.py derives every rate and period from them. Do not round.

planets.source: E. M. Standish, JPL Solar System Dynamics, 'Approximate Positions of the Planets', Table 1: Keplerian elements and their rates, J2000 ecliptic and equinox, valid 1800 AD - 2050 AD (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html). L is the mean longitude at J2000.0 (deg), L_rate its rate (deg per Julian century); e is the eccentricity. The Earth's row is the Earth-Moon barycentre (EM Bary).

moon.source: IERS Conventions (2003), IERS Technical Note 32, fundamental arguments from Simon et al. (1994), A&A 282, 663, as coded in ERFA (liberfa/erfa: src/faf03.c, src/faom03.c, src/fapa03.c). The Moon's mean longitude L = F + Omega, referred to the mean equinox of date; its sidereal rate is L's rate less the general precession in longitude p_A. Coefficients in arcseconds (F, Omega) and radians (p_A), t in Julian centuries since J2000.0. Only the terms linear in t are used: a geared Moon turns at a constant rate.

check.source: NASA Goddard (NSSDC) fact sheets, read as a cross-check only (not used by make.py): Saturn's sidereal orbit period 10 755.699 d (make.py derives 10 755.884 d from Standish's rate, 17 ppm apart); the Planetary Fact Sheet's rounded orbital periods (Mercury 88.0, Venus 224.7, Earth 365.2, Moon 27.3, Mars 687.0 d) agree with the derived ones to their rounding.
